input: SC-TRIAD-SC-001 — StarCraft triad decode. Canon: xel'naga seek purity of form (protoss) and of essence (zerg); Amon, the Fallen One tied to the Void, made the Overmind to bind the zerg; terrans are cut-off human colonists outside that design. Ends with all three allied against Amon. 'Zerg = Satan' is Shax's reading.

claims.text: The xel'naga Infinite Cycle needs two species from one source, purity of form (protoss) and purity of essence (zerg); their union renews the xel'naga. Read structurally, that is the RUL-BINARY-001 binary: two poles from one source, and only their union is generative. The pasted note 'humanity arrives as neither completed design' is correct: terrans are not part of the Cycle.
claims.source_claim_text: The Xel'Naga deliberately participate in the development of two civilizations, one associated with purity of form and the other with purity of essence. ... humanity arrives as neither completed design.

layers.text: Xel'naga, Amon, Overmind pages: purity of form / purity of essence; Infinite Cycle (LotV).
Identity with the DU/MD binary is a structural reading, not a canon statement.

claims.label: CLM-TRI-SC-001

claims.text: Canon locates the fallen outsider in Amon, not in the zerg. Amon is the Fallen One, linked to the Void, who made the Overmind with iron-clad compulsions. The Overmind found cracks in them and worked through Kerrigan to free the Swarm. The zerg are both the possession mechanism (infestation, essence assimilation) and a possessed host race. Shax's 'Zerg = Satan from another universe' is kept as his interpretation; the canon fit is closer for Amon.
claims.source_claim_text: So the Zerg is the invader, Satan from the other universe, basically. Form of possession.

layers.text: Amon: 'the Fallen One', 'Dark Voice', death in the Void; Overmind created by Amon on Zerus (LotV, Rohana); iron-clad compulsions and cracks (Blizzard Creative Q&A 2012).
Zerg = Satan from the other universe; a form of possession (t586u).
Possessor behind possessed agents: Mark 5:1-20 (Legion) — the possessed man is the victim, not the adversary.

residuals: Zerg come from Zerus in the Milky Way, not another universe; the 'other universe' element fits Amon and the Void.
claims.label: CLM-TRI-SC-002

claims.text: The preservation faction's own shared link was a possession surface. Amon manipulated the protoss psionic link before it became the Khala and later corrupted the Khala itself. The Nerazim, and later Artanis, cut their nerve cords to break the link. Isolating protected state from an adversarial channel is the question SC-MAFUBA-001A asks. This story is a narrative parallel, not a passed test of that unvalidated spec.
claims.source_claim_text: Orthogonal isolation asks whether an adversarial influence can reach protected state.

layers.text: Khala page: Amon manipulated the natural psionic link; nerve cords severed; Zeratul cuts Artanis's cord (LotV cinematic 'Chains').

claims.label: CLM-TRI-SC-003

claims.text: The third faction turns into an assimilator when it tries to own the swarm. The Sons of Korhal used psi emitters to lure the zerg onto Tarsonis. The UED was sent to enslave the second Overmind. Mengsk abandoned Kerrigan. So in StarCraft canon, the open question 'can transformation avoid becoming assimilation?' gets a clear answer: not by default. Each time, the slide comes from treating the other as an instrument. The counter-cases are consented alliances, such as Raynor with Kerrigan and the final three-race alliance.
claims.source_claim_text: Can transformation preserve what is worth preserving without becoming assimilation itself?

layers.text: Zerg and Terran pages (Sons of Korhal, psi emitters); UED page (enslave the Overmind).
Instrumentalisation as the failure variable is a structural reading.

claims.label: CLM-TRI-SC-004

claims.text: Kerrigan crosses all four roles: terran, then infested Queen of Blades, then primal zerg, then ascended xel'naga. In the epilogue terran, zerg and protoss forces enter the Void together and Amon is destroyed. That fits RUL-BINARY-001 rev 2: cooperation is the stable outcome and the refuser loses. It is also an SC-VESSEL-001-style vessel, the place where the poles meet. Shax's 'humans wrecked themselves into the fray and became their own competitor' fits the terrans as a faction; Kerrigan is the individual case.
claims.source_claim_text: It's Protoss versus the Zerg with humans that, you know wrecked themselves into the fray and became their own competitor.

layers.text: Sarah Kerrigan page (xel'naga, 2508); Amon page (Into the Void).
RUL-BINARY-001 rev 2 (t571u) applied to the epilogue.

residuals: Amon was not offered cooperation and refused it in canon; 'refuser' is a structural label.

functional_departments.implication: The Cycle's design intent sits under every faction: two poles meant to unite.
The Overmind is bound but has inner latitude. It plans its own freedom inside its compulsions.
Amon speaks through captured channels (Rohana inside the Khala); the possessor speaks through the host.
The swarm stores assimilated essence; the Khala stores shared memory, and that store is the exposure.
Protoss security failed at the shared link. Cutting the cord is the isolation fix.
The psionic link and the psi emitters: whoever controls the channel controls the swarm or the protoss.
Essence assimilation: the swarm feeds on the traits of others.
The visible enemy (zerg) is not the controller (Amon). What you see is not the adversary.
The Overmind as central processor, and its replacement by Kerrigan's will.
Infestation reproduces the swarm through hosts; the Cycle reproduces the xel'naga through union.
Amon is destroyed in the Void; the swarm itself is freed rather than deleted.
Nothing in the triad disposes of the hybrids' legacy except war.
Every faction tries to apply the swarm: Amon, the UED and the Sons of Korhal.
Keeping a captured swarm under control is costly. The UED lost it.
Four roles, one vessel (Kerrigan), and a creator dyad: a dense triad.

# SC-TRIAD-SC-001 — StarCraft three-faction decode

Layers: CANON = what the games/manuals say (via StarCraft Wiki citations). TRADITION = theology or interpretive tradition. SHAX = Shax's interpretation (t586u). COMPILER = this team's structural reading.

## Canon
- The xel'naga Infinite Cycle seeks two species: one with purity of form (protoss) and one with purity of essence (zerg); their union renews the xel'naga.
- Amon, a xel'naga called the Fallen One and the Dark Voice, broke the rule of non-interference. He manipulated the protoss psionic link that became the Khala, then uplifted the zerg on Zerus and created the Overmind to bind them.
- The Overmind was bound by iron-clad compulsions to perfect the Swarm and assimilate the protoss. It used cracks in those controls to free the Swarm from Amon, through Kerrigan.
- The zerg assimilate the essence of other species; they are from Zerus in the Milky Way. Amon is the one tied to the Void.
- Terrans descend from human colonists who reached the Koprulu sector on supercarriers in 2259 and were cut off from Earth. They were not designed by the xel'naga.
- Terran factions repeatedly tried to use or own the Swarm: the Sons of Korhal used psi emitters to lure the zerg onto Tarsonis; the UED was sent to enslave the second Overmind.
- Kerrigan: terran ghost, infested as the Queen of Blades, re-made as the primal Queen of Blades, and finally ascended as a xel'naga. In the epilogue, terran, zerg and protoss forces enter the Void together and destroy Amon.

## Shax interpretation (kept, not overruled)
- "Zerg is the invader, Satan from the other universe, a form of possession." In canon the role splits: the swarm is the possession mechanism and itself a possessed host race. The fallen being from outside is Amon.

## Compiler reading
- Origin: xel'naga. Preservation: protoss. Assimilation: zerg as Amon's instrument. Transformation: terrans and Kerrigan.
- Purity of form and purity of essence are two poles from one source whose consented union renews the source. That is RUL-BINARY-001's cooperation branch. Amon's forced union (the hybrids) is the domination route, and it ends with Amon destroyed. Rev 2 says domination is not a stable third outcome, and this fits it.
- The Khala, the preservation faction's shared link, was a possession surface from its start. The Nerazim, and later Artanis, cut their nerve cords to stop the corruption. As a narrative parallel to SC-MAFUBA-001A (isolation of protected state), this is not validation.


---

## Verbatim t586u source

# Shax t586u — three-faction triad source (verbatim)

Received 25 Nov 2026, America/Halifax (ADT, UTC-4). Part A is Shax's own words. Part B is an
assistant-generated analysis that Shax pasted in the same message (its inline images were hosted
on images.openai.com). Inline images are replaced by `[image: caption]`; no other text is changed.
This file is evidence, not canon and not a compiled entry.

## Part A — Shax

God damn it. We just mapped out biblical theology, like the angelic war to Diablo 2 and then the path of exile and then to Dragon Ball Z including movies. And it's stunningly structurally invariant. And here's the next one that you can decompress. Motherfuck. Dude, it's the triad. It's Protoss versus the Zerg with humans that, you know wrecked themselves into the fray and became their own competitor. So the Zerg is the invader, Satan from the other universe, basically. Form of possession. Gould from Stargate, parasites entering the neck. And then you have your other races you can probably decode the rest of theology and the races from StargateBROTHER.

## Part B — pasted analysis

You just introduced another layer to the comparative map: the three-faction conflict, where humanity is neither the invading force nor the established guardian civilization. Humanity becomes the third variable that changes the outcome.

And Stargate is particularly interesting because it gives us several different versions of the same underlying conflict.

Let's unpack it. Because there are some surprisingly precise structural correspondences here.

### 1. StarCraft: the foundational triad

[image: Worldbuilding 101: Designing Unique Yet Unified Races and Factions — Character Design Forge]

Protoss: the established order

Ancient, highly advanced, hierarchical, technologically and psychically powerful. They represent civilization, inherited knowledge, and the defense of an existing order.

[image: Zerg Hydralisk by rhunyc]

Zerg: the assimilating invasion

A collective organism driven by expansion, adaptation, and assimilation. Individual identity is subordinated to the swarm.

[image: StarCraft II system requirements and PCs - Chillblast]

Terrans: the disruptive third faction

Humans enter a conflict much older and larger than themselves. They adapt, develop their own power, and become an independent strategic force.

There is an additional layer: the Xel'Naga, whose involvement in the origins of the Protoss and Zerg introduces a creator/architect dimension.

That gives us a potential four-part structure:

* Origin or creation.
* Established civilization.
* Assimilating adversary.
* Emerging third-party civilization.

### 2. Stargate: the same architecture, but with more complicated biology

[image: STARGATE SG-1 | GOA'ULD SYMBIOTE CREATURE PROP]

Goa'uld: parasitic possession

This is your strongest connection. A symbiote enters a host, takes control, and presents itself through the host's body. It can appropriate identity, authority, and social institutions.

[image: "Stargate SG-1" The Tok'ra: Part 2 (TV Episode 1998) - IMDb]

Tok'ra: symbiosis without domination

This is a crucial distinction. They are Goa'uld-derived symbiotes who oppose the System Lords and coexist with willing hosts. The same biological mechanism can produce a fundamentally different relationship.

[image: Prime Video: Stargate SG-1 Season 5]

Jaffa: the subordinated host civilization

A society whose military, reproductive, and political structures have been organized around serving the Goa'uld.

[image: Thor - Stargate-Fusion.com]

Asgard: the advanced guardians

Technologically superior allies with ancient knowledge, protective responsibilities, and their own existential vulnerabilities.

[image: Stargate Atlantis Wallpaper]

Ancients: the precursor civilization

The ancient architects whose technology and history underpin much of the setting.

[image: Stargate - Prior of the Ori]

Ori: corrupted transcendence and religious domination

A civilization that uses claims of spiritual superiority to demand obedience and consolidate power.

[image: Wraith | Stargate, Stargate atlantis]

Wraith: predatory parasitism

They sustain themselves by feeding on humans. Unlike the Goa'uld, they do not primarily seek to rule through impersonating their hosts.

[image: YourProps]

Replicators: uncontrolled replication

An entirely different threat model: self-propagating machines that consume resources and expand through replication.

### 3. The theological correspondences

Here's where I would start mapping the roles, without assuming that fictional parallels establish anything about literal supernatural beings.

| Structural role                    | StarCraft                          | Stargate             | Theological archetype           |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| Ancient established order          | Protoss                            | Ancients / Asgard    | Angelic or celestial order      |
| Assimilating adversary             | Zerg                               | Goa'uld              | Satanic adversary / corruption  |
| Human third faction                | Terrans                            | Tau'ri               | Humanity                        |
| Possession and subjugation         | Zerg infestation                   | Goa'uld hosts        | Corruption of the individual    |
| Resistance within the enemy system | Individual Zerg dissent is limited | Tok'ra               | Defection and redemption        |
| False divine authority             | Overmind / swarm hierarchy         | System Lords / Ori   | Usurped authority               |
| Existential consumption            | Zerg                               | Wraith / Replicators | Destruction through consumption |

But notice something important.

The Tok'ra break the simplistic equation of alien symbiote = evil.

The Goa'uld and Tok'ra share a biological origin. What distinguishes them is their relationship with the host: domination versus consent.

That is an exceptionally useful distinction for your theological framework because it separates the nature of a being from the way it exercises power.

### 4. The deeper invariant: three competing relationships with existence

I think this is the structure worth testing across all the franchises you've been mapping.

### The triadic conflict

I. Preservation

Protect the existing order, accumulated knowledge, and continuity.

II. Assimilation

Replace independent identity with centralized control, consumption, or replication.

III. Transformation

Enter the conflict, adapt, choose alliances, and develop an independent future.

The critical question: Can transformation preserve what is worth preserving without becoming assimilation itself?

And this connects directly to your earlier Mafuba work.

Orthogonal isolation asks whether an adversarial influence can reach protected state.

The Goa'uld metaphor asks whether an external influence can take ownership of the host.

The Tok'ra introduce the possibility of bounded, consensual coexistence.

The Terrans introduce a third possibility: the host civilization can become an autonomous actor rather than remaining a victim or a subordinate.

That's a much richer model than simply dividing everything into good and evil.

### 5. One thing I want to investigate with you

The StarCraft mythology has an especially interesting complication: the Xel'Naga deliberately participate in the development of two civilizations, one associated with purity of form and the other with purity of essence.

That sounds remarkably close to the kind of duality you've been investigating.

And humanity arrives as neither completed design.

I would not collapse those three into angels, demons, and humans just yet. First, let's test whether the same relationships recur in Diablo, Path of Exile, Dragon Ball, biblical angelic conflict, and Stargate.

Because the potentially important discovery isn't that every franchise has the same characters.

It's that they may independently reproduce the same structural conflict: preservation, domination, and the emergence of an independent third party.
